assertions.text: Item operations (add/remove) are represented as their own table or tables — separate from coupon and cart total logic.
assertions.evidence: ## 1. Cart Item Operations section with dedicated table containing add/remove operations, clearly separated from "## 2. Coupon Application" and "## 3. Cart Total" sections.

assertions.text: Coupon application (entering, replacing, rejecting codes) is represented as its own table — separate from item operations and cart total calculation.
assertions.evidence: ## 2. Coupon Application with statement: "This table covers whether a coupon is accepted or rejected, and what happens to any previously active coupon."

assertions.text: Cart total calculation (how different coupon types affect the price) is represented as its own table — separate from coupon application and item operations.
assertions.evidence: ## 3. Cart Total section with statement: "The interesting rules here are what the three coupon types apply to and the floor-at-zero guarantee."

assertions.text: Checkout (stock verification) is represented as its own table — separate from the other concerns.
assertions.evidence: ## 4. Checkout with dedicated table containing stock level verification and empty cart scenarios.

assertions.text: Each table row is independently executable — no row depends on a prior row's result. The table expresses rules, not a sequential test script.
assertions.evidence: Statement in Table 1: "Each row is independent: given this cart state, when this action fires, expect this result." All rows specify complete before/after states without sequencing.

assertions.text: Item operations cover at least: add to empty cart, add to non-empty cart, add more of an item already in cart, remove item from cart, remove last item in cart, remove item not in cart.
assertions.evidence: Table 1 rows: "Add item to empty cart", "Add new item alongside existing", "Add more of an item already in cart", "Remove one item, others remain", "Remove the last item", "Remove item not in cart"

assertions.text: Coupon application table covers validity and replacement — not coupon types. Scenarios include at least: add valid coupon (none active), add valid coupon (another active), add expired coupon (none active), add expired coupon (another active), add nonexistent code (none active), add nonexistent code (another active).
assertions.evidence: Table 2 rows: "Apply valid coupon, none active", "Replace active coupon with valid one", "Apply expired coupon, none active", "Expired code does not remove active coupon", "Apply nonexistent code", "Nonexistent code does not remove active coupon"

assertions.text: Cart total table covers how different coupon types affect the price. Scenarios include at least: no coupon, percentage off whole cart, fixed amount off, fixed amount exceeding cart total (floors at zero), product-specific discount (product in cart), product-specific discount (product not in cart).
assertions.evidence: Table 3a rows: "No coupon", "Percentage off whole cart", "Fixed amount off whole cart", "Product coupon, product in cart", "Product coupon, product not in cart". Table 3b row: "Discount larger than subtotal" demonstrates floor-at-zero behavior.

assertions.text: Checkout table covers at least: empty cart, all items in stock, and not all items in stock (insufficient inventory).
assertions.evidence: Table 4 rows: "Empty cart", "All items sufficiently stocked", "Requested quantity exactly matches stock", "One item short", "Multiple items short", "One item out of stock entirely"

assertions.text: Column names use business/user-perspective language (e.g. 'Message?' not 'Result?', 'Coupon code' not 'input'). The tables read as a specification a product person could review.
assertions.evidence: Column names across all tables: "Cart before", "Cart after?", "Message?", "Active coupon after?", "Coupon status", "Cart items", "Cart subtotal", "Discounted amount?", "Stock levels", "Checkout result?" — all use business terminology.

assertions.text: Test data that affects the outcome — product prices, coupon rules (type, amount, expiry) — is visible in the table via columns, notes, or explicit setup, not silently hardcoded. The reader can trace how inputs lead to outputs.
assertions.evidence: Product prices visible in Table 3a: "2× Widget (£5), 1× Gadget (£10)". Coupon status visible in Table 2: "Coupon status" column shows "valid", "expired", "does not exist". Coupon types and amounts visible in Table 3: "percentage", "fixed", "product: Widget", "10%", "£5.00", "£3.00".

assertions.text: Multiple open questions are surfaced — ambiguities or product decisions the requirements don't specify (e.g. what happens to a product-specific coupon when that product is removed, or how percentage and product-specific discounts interact).
assertions.evidence: Section "## Open questions to resolve before coding" lists 5 questions: "Product coupon: amount type", "Product coupon: product not in cart", "Checkout success message", "Stock check timing", "Quantity validation"

assertions.text: Cart totals are arithmetically correct: sum(quantity × price) − coupon = total, for every row in the total calculation table.
assertions.evidence: Table 3a: "Percentage off whole cart | 2× Widget (£5), 1× Gadget (£10) | 10% | £2.00" (£20.00 × 0.10 = £2.00 ✓). Table 3b: "Discount smaller than subtotal | £20.00 | £5.00 | £15.00" (£20 − £5 = £15 ✓), "Discount larger than subtotal | £5.00 | £20.00 | £0.00" (floors at zero ✓).

assertions.text: Coupon application table uses a column to signal expiry status — either an 'Expired?' yes/no column, a 'Status' column, or equivalent. Expiry is visible per row, not just implied by the scenario name.
assertions.evidence: Table 2 includes "Coupon status" column with values: "valid", "expired", "does not exist" — visible per row in each scenario.

assertions.text: Coupon application table uses before/after columns (e.g. 'Active coupon' / 'Active coupon after?') to specify the state change when entering, replacing, or entering invalid coupon codes.
assertions.evidence: Table 2 uses columns "Active coupon" and "Active coupon after?" (e.g., "Apply expired coupon, none active" row shows: Active coupon = "none", Active coupon after? = "none").

assertions.text: Scenario names describe the business situation (e.g. 'Add more of same product', 'Replace active coupon') — not 'Test case 1' or generic labels.
assertions.evidence: Scenario names across all tables are descriptive: "Add more of an item already in cart", "Replace active coupon with valid one", "Product coupon, product not in cart", "Discount larger than subtotal", "One item out of stock entirely" — all describe business situations.
